I was expecting that WYSIWYG would be because it is wondering how it is akin to what is the reader or what perhaps an agent session would be. With the different runs visualized, and that components can be of code and can be of data as well. For instance, a [holon] is drawn and it already holds kinds of things in it. I hope that is as data. And I expect WYSIWYG to I've been thinking about the reader, because the reader is where somewhere I started as well. There is some information about the intersection which is being matched against a component. And the Chrome that comes with that. Naturally being able to edit that in place. That's part of WYSIWYG. I don't know how much it is an editor. As it is edit in place, in a way. The context menu. The actions. Don't know if that has a place yet. Of course, to be able to edit data nicely. Because adding a node is something that has the trigger which is part of the component definition as well. So it then actually runs a program. And that program run or to be visible as well. But I feel like the inspector panel and the data viewer are still locked away from me. I'm expecting the fully immersive approach.

And I think field viewer, of course, changes. It's just that you change the root component. And therefore, you're just spawning cards for each level. List, and the element naturally that becomes for each child is auto-matched by components, because components define the type [they take]. There is whatever is selected. The idea about the whole [holarchy] viewer, I guess, is also a possibility. Then it sounds like there is centrally an address. For where you are. That syncs across these. Interesting.
body.title: Fully immersive
